messages:
nina_reps: starting handoff for MeridianCare POC. They want a private deploy into their AWS account, strict logging with original client IPs, egress through their corporate TLS-inspect proxy, and a short cost estimate for the POC. Can neteng & sec advise on topology + firewall rules?
omar_neteng: quick summary: three viable topologies: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoints) 1 easiest to manage, minimal route churn but loses client src IPs. 2) VPC Peering / Transit Gateway 1 preserves client IPs but needs routing attachments, peering limits, and possibly TGW fees. 3) PrivateLink + in-VPC forwarder/NAT that records src IPs into X-Forwarded-For (requires app changes).
claire_se: adding operational notes: PrivateLink is best for customers who cannot allow inbound peering or TGW attachments. If MeridianCare insists on src IP for security logging, recommend TGW/peering. Also ask whether their SIEM expects original IPs or if app-level header is acceptable.
ina_reps: they said logs must contain orig client IPs for throttling. So peering/TGW preferred. Any firewall snippets we can send them?
dinesh_finance: budget ballpark for a low-volume POC (30 days, <200 rps):
- PrivateLink: one-time setup + feature add-on (~$1kquote placeholder), minor infra hours.
- Peering/TGW: minimal product charge but more SWEs/time (~$2keng time) + their TGW/attachment fees.
These are roughs; we'll issue a formal quote after network design.
tina_info_sec: security checklist: if we do peering/TGW -> require cross-account IAM role proof, VPN or Direct Connect for onprem, and peering acceptance window. For PrivateLink -> ensure we provide ENI CIDRs and cert thumbprint for mTLS validation. If TLS-inspect is used, mutual TLS will break unless they whitelist our endpoint CA or provide cert passthrough.
omar_neteng: firewall / SG example to share (customer side):

```
# Customer outbound rules for PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
- ALLOW TCP 443 -> <our ENI CIDR list>
- ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 -> <our ENI CIDR list>  # ephemeral ports from client
- ALLOW UDP 53 -> <their resolver>
# For Peering/TGW to our service VPC (preserves src IP)
- ALLOW TCP 443 -> <our service ALB/NLB IPs>
- ALLOW ICMP Type 3/Fragmentation -> monitor PMTU
```

(we'll supply exact IP lists per region).
claire_se: note re: MTU & TLS-inspect: customers that route to a TLS-inspect proxy often see MTU/MSS issues; run a PMTU/tracepath early. If they terminate TLS and re-initiate to us, mutual TLS will fail unless we rely on token-based auth.
nina_reps: customer question: does traffic through their proxy change our egress charges or latency SLO?
dinesh_finance: billing notes: our egress billing is based on bytes leaving our infra to customer endpoints; if traffic goes through their proxy inside their network, our billing unchanged. However, their internal bandwidth and egress (if proxy goes out to internet) are their cost. Latency SLOs could be affected if proxy adds significant processing; callout in SLO docs.
omar_neteng: ops checklist for kickoff call:
- provide customer VPC CIDRs + intended AZs
- confirm whether they allow TGW peering attachments or prefer PrivateLink
- firewall admin contact + testing window
- whether they perform TLS inspect and can do cert passthrough
deploy_bot: ticket NET-7890 created: generate ENI CIDR allocation + produce region IP list (assignee: omar_neteng).
tina_info_sec: security Qs to answer before kickoff: which compliance boundaries (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/PCI)? If HIPAA/PCI in scope, we'll need to document data flows and KMS/HSM integration for private deployments.
claire_se: I'll draft a 1-page tradeoff doc (Peering vs PrivateLink vs NAT-forwarder) and include TLS-inspect impact.
nina_reps: proposed next steps: 1) schedule 30m with MeridianCare + neteng/sec this week, 2) omar to post ENI IP list + SG examples in this thread by EOD tomorrow, 3) dinesh to prep POC budget estimate note. I'll ping customer for CIDRs and proxy owner.
meridian_proxy_admin: (customer) thanks, will collect VPC CIDRs and confirm whether TLS inspect is inline. We'll respond by EOD tomorrow.
